The Zaporozhian Sich had 12,000 to 20,000 Cossacks during its practically independent period of 1657 to 1687.
The Republic of Maryland in West Africa had 900 to 1,000 settlers in 1851.
William Lane's New Australia began with 238 people, and about 2,000 descendants live in Paraguay.
zones_new.essay:
A settler republic forms when people move past the edge of a state's control and set up their own government there. The cases here share a pattern: land where a state's claim was weak, a group with enough guns or money to stay, and a later decision by a stronger power.

Southern Africa has the fullest list. Boers, Dutch-speaking settlers, left the British Cape Colony in the 1830s in part over language laws and compensation for slaves. Retief wrote in 1837 that they expected to govern themselves without interference. Natalia lasted from 1839 to 1843 before Britain annexed it. Britain then recognised the South African Republic by the Sand River Convention of 1852 and the Orange Free State in 1854, the second after a Bloemfontein meeting had voted to stay British. Those two lasted about fifty years, until the war of 1899 to 1902. Smaller states came from deals with African rulers: Stellaland from land paid to mercenaries, Upingtonia from a purchase, Klein Vrystaat from what the Swazi king thought was a grazing concession. Each was absorbed within a few years.

North America followed the same order. Watauga wrote its own compact in 1772, Vermont stayed out for fourteen years, and Franklin ran courts and paid salaries in deer hides before North Carolina took back control. The Constitution then closed the way: Article IV bars forming a new state inside another without consent. California's Bear Flag lasted under a month and Hawaii's republic four years, and both ended in US control.

Colonisation societies are a variant in which a private body funded the move. The Mississippi and Maryland societies, set up partly by slaveholders wishing to remove free Black people, founded colonies on the West African coast that later joined Liberia. Their settlers took power over the Indigenous people. Others left to escape politics at home: New Australia and Nueva Germania got land from Paraguay, and split or failed within a few years.

Cossack hosts are the oldest form. Runaways settled the steppe between Russia, Poland and the Crimean Khanate and sold their military service to each. The Zaporozhian Sich was practically independent from 1657 to 1687, and Catherine the Great disbanded it in 1775.

This route depended on land that no strong state yet held. Those frontiers are gone: almost all land is now claimed, and international law lets only states acquire the little that remains. The sources also show who paid for it. Many of these republics were built on land taken from peoples who already lived there.

sources.t: Sand River Convention, text, Reitz appendix

odds.why: These are estimates from the record. Moving a group and buying land is still possible, so money is the highest figure: Maryland drew on a state grant and New Australia on members' savings. Building a state on that land is rare now, because nearly all land is claimed. Law is low because a host's law applies from arrival, and a new state inside a US state needs consent. Past cases held for a few years to fifty, and recognition came only from a colonial power withdrawing, as in 1852 and 1854.

own.own_why: You get a farm or a town inside someone's country, as at Nueva Germania or New Australia, because Paraguay gave the land and later dissolved the cooperative. The separate law and courts of Vermont or the Transvaal came from an edge of empire that does not exist any longer, so the figure is well below the unrecognised-state route.

zones_new.name: Religious states and military orders
zones_new.who_owns: Almost none of these survive as territories. Their lands became part of other countries, and the groups that held on did so as ordinary corporations or private landowners under the host's law.

rules.says: Emperor Frederick II granted and confirmed the Teutonic Order's right to conquer and acquire land in Prussia. One historian argues it was backdated from 1235.
Poland and the Grand Master ended their war. Albert of Hohenzollern resigned as Grand Master and became Duke of a new secular Prussia, ending the order's state there.
A religious duty is no defence to a criminal bigamy law, since excusing it would permit every citizen to become a law unto himself.

rules.cite: Late Corporation of the LDS Church v. United States, 136 U.S. 1 (1890)
rules.says: Upheld the Edmunds-Tucker Act, which dissolved the church's corporation and allowed seizure of its property. Assets were released in 1893 after the church stopped polygamy.

zones_new.hook: Anything a stronger neighbour wants. Hospitaller Rhodes fell to 100,000 men, Canudos to a national army, Munster to its bishop's siege. Inside modern countries, general law wins: Reynolds and the 1890 ruling show a government can reach belief-driven practice and even the church's property.
zones_new.can_you_build: A religious group can buy land and live by its rules under general law, as the Harmony Society, Amana and Zion did. Those that went further used conquest, and then lost it to larger conquest or left it to a charter from a ruler who could take it back.
facts: The Teutonic Order bought Estonia from Denmark in 1346 for 19,000 Cologne marks.
The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom reached areas with nearly 30 million people before Qing and allied forces ended it in 1864.
Estimates of the dead at Canudos run from 5,000 to about 30,000.
The Harmony Society lasted 100 years and had a net worth of US$1.2 million when it dissolved in 1905.
King Andrew II of Hungary expelled the Teutonic Knights from Burzenland in 1225 for trying to answer only to the Pope.
zones_new.essay:
Religion has given several groups a reason and a discipline to run territory, and for centuries some rulers accepted that. Three forms appear in the record.

The first is the military order: monks who were also soldiers. A ruler or the Pope gave them a frontier, usually in exchange for fighting. Hungary granted the Burzenland to the Teutonic Knights in 1211 with the right to hold markets and courts, then expelled them in 1225 after they tried to answer only to the Pope. They then won Prussia through the Golden Bull of Rimini and ruled there until 1525. The Hospitallers took Rhodes by force in 1310, held it for 212 years, lost it to Suleiman in 1522, and got Malta as a fief from Charles V in 1530 until Napoleon removed them in 1798. These are the longest holds in this group, with the protection of the Church and support of Christian kings. The Sovereign Military Order of Malta, a separate entry, is what remains.

The second is the religious uprising. Anabaptists seized Munster in 1534 and fell in June 1535. The Taiping held Nanjing for a decade and were defeated with foreign help. Antonio Conselheiro's followers at Canudos beat three army expeditions and were destroyed by the fourth in 1897. The Imamate of Oman lasted the longest, with elected imams on and off from about 750 until a war with the Sultan, who had British support, ended in 1959. The Caucasian Imamate lasted until Shamil's capture in 1859. Scale and tactics varied, and most of these ended by a larger state's army.

The third is the religious community inside a country, which claims no state. Harmony, Zoar, Amana and Bishop Hill bought land in the United States and held goods in common. They lasted decades, and ended through ageing, debt or a vote. Some tried for more. Nauvoo's charter gave Joseph Smith's city a militia of at least 2,500 and a court that freed him on habeas corpus. He was killed in 1844, and his followers were expelled by 1846. James Strang's followers took over Beaver Island's local offices, with Strang crowned in 1850 and killed in 1856. The US Supreme Court then ruled in Reynolds and in the 1890 church case that religious duty does not override general law.

The record suggests that charters came from rulers who needed soldiers on a frontier that no longer exists, and that later attempts inside modern states were overruled.

sources.t: State of the Teutonic Order, Wikipedia
Late Corporation of the LDS Church v. United States, Wikipedia
Free Speech Center, MTSU: Late Corporation case

odds.why: These are estimates from the record. A religious community can buy land and build, as Harmony and Amana did, so building and money are relatively high. Law is low because Reynolds and the 1890 church case hold that religious duty does not override general law. Holding separate power was possible for orders with a king's or the Pope's backing, and nearly all others fell to an army. Recognition is rare and came with old grants, such as those to the Teutonic Order and the Hospitallers.

own.own_why: You get a town with shared property and strict rules under general law, like Zoar or Zion, but not your own courts, because the 1879 and 1890 US rulings put general law first and modern hosts do not hand out fiefs. A mass movement with arms, the second figure, can take territory, as the Taiping and Caucasian Imamate did, but those ended with defeat by a larger army.
